title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-maya
content:
Purpose:
- Scratchpad for Lumina Retail outreach + partnership angle. Account research, messaging drafts, objection handling, next steps.

Account snapshot (internal notes):
- Company: Lumina Retail (mid-market omnichannel retailer)
- Approx: 120 stores, 2500 employees, $850M ARR (public/press signals)
- Tech stack hints: AWS-hosted storefront + data lake, React frontend, using Snowflake + Redshift for analytics.
- Signals: Hiring for Head of ML and Recommendations (LinkedIn job posts), announcement about personalization initiative in Q4 2025.
- Current inference footprint hypothesis: in-house models for recommendations and chat support (likely PyTorch on EC2 or SageMaker endpoints).
- Pain we can address: expensive per-token costs for chat, tail latency on on-demand recs, need for private deployment for PII, desire to reduce infra ops overhead while keeping SLAs.

Key contacts (to verify before outreach):
- Sara Patel — CTO (senior exec, product/infra leaning)
- Ethan Gomez — Head of ML (likely technical buyer)
- Priya Bhandari — Head of Product (influence on roadmap)
- SDR notes: reach out to Ethan first (technical), cc Priya for product fit; Sara for exec sponsor after initial interest.

Top value props (pick 1–2 per outreach):
- Reduce per-inference unit cost via batching, KV caching, and model quantization recommendations.
- Predictable latency + SLA with Dedicated pools (good for real-time recs).
- Private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) for regulated customer PII and audit logs.
- Single API/SDK across hosted/dedicated/private — less rework for platform teams.

Outbound email drafts (A/B test):
A) Short cold outreach (technical):
Subject: Cut inference cost and stabilize latency for Lumina personalization
Hi {{first_name}},
Saw the personalization push at Lumina — quick question: what’s your typical p99 latency for product recs and how are you handling spiky traffic from campaigns?
We’ve helped retail platforms reduce inference unit costs 2–3x and keep 99th percentile latency within 100–200ms using a mix of dedicated GPU pools, caching, and model variants. If helpful I can share a short cost/latency playbook tailored to your stack.
— Maya

B) Executive/partnership angle:
Subject: Partnership idea to accelerate Lumina’s personalization roadmap
Hi Sara,
Congrats on the personalization initiative. We work with retailers to decouple model ops from infra — offering reserved capacity and private deployments so teams can ship faster without operating a full inference stack.
Would love 20 minutes to discuss a partnership pilot (we can run a small benchmark and cost comparison).
Best,
Maya

Follow-up template (after 3–5 days):
Subject: Quick follow-up on personalization + cost playbook
Hi {{first_name}},
Wanted to follow up on my note — happy to send a 1-page cost/latency comparison vs. your current setup. Any chance you’re the right contact or can point me to who owns Recommendations/Infra?

Call script / discovery checklist (aim for 20–30 min):
- Quick intro (2 min) — who owns the problem and SLA targets.
- Current infra: model hosting (SageMaker/EC2/GKE), average qps, p95/p99 latency, sequence lengths, batch sizes.
- Cost baseline: token/inference cost, monthly spend on inference.
- Constraints: PCI/PII, VPC requirements, audit/KMS needs, compliance (SOC2/HIPAA?).
- Ops pain: model rollouts, canarying, debugging latency spikes.
- Win criteria: 20–30% cost reduction OR p99 improvement to target X ms OR simplified ops (fewer infra tickets).
- Agree next step: benchmark run or intro to infra eng for network/security review.

Common objections + suggested responses:
1) "We’re already on OpenAI / managed endpoints"
- Response: Great — many customers use managed models for experiments. For production recs we offer deterministic latency and unit-cost controls with private/dedicated options; we can run a side-by-side cost and latency comparison using your traffic profile.

2) "We have strict data residency / PII rules"
- Response: We support Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. We can scope a pilot under your network/IT constraints.

3) "We don’t want vendor lock-in"
- Response: Redwood provides compatibility with open model variants and a consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private — you can fallback between tiers and pin model versions. Emphasize exit-friendly configs and exportable logs/metrics.

4) "Not a priority / budget cycle"
- Response: Offer a lightweight pilot that demonstrates cost savings with minimal engineering time (we can run a bench with your sample traces, ~2–4 weeks). Frame as a low-risk experiment.

Benchmark idea (what to offer in pilot):
- Small benchmark comparing current model endpoints vs Redwood Dedicated and a quantized model variant. Metrics: throughput (qps), p95/p99 latency, cost per 1M inferences, and degradation cases under traffic spikes. Deliverable: one-pager + dashboard + short exec summary.

Notes / to-dos before outreach:
- Verify Ethan’s LinkedIn + email (work address).
- Run quick pricing calc for Lumina: estimate 10M monthly inference tokens, current cost assumptions (ask Jordan for recent retail averages).
- Prepare 1-page cost/latency playbook (use template in Confluence: CONFLUENCE-UI/partner-playbook).
- Get infra/security FAQ from Priya (list of common network/IT questions).

Next steps (owner):
- Maya: draft 1-pager + A/B email sequences (due 2026-02-24).
- Jordan: confirm pricing baseline and add example benchmarks (due 2026-02-27).
- Priya: compile security checklist (due 2026-03-01).

Scratch / random ideas:
- Offer co-marketing: joint case study if pilot meets cost/latency goals.
- Invite Lumina to closed beta for a new caching feature (reduce cold-starts for recs) — good hook for exec intro.
- Prepare a short Loom explaining Dedicated vs Private deployments targeted at infra teams.

End of notes.
